feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear positioning for senior digital communications roles and credible progression within one organization. It reads professionally and shows solid scope, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition, and tighter structure across overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility: long tenure at NACo with promotions, large-scale website migration, analytics stack ownership, and studio build-out all signal real responsibility.  
- Writing is generally polished and readable, with strong action verbs and relevant technical/detail balance for this field.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style consistency: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; add serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); “cross-channel” vs “Multi-channel” is a minor style inconsistency. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It reads clearly, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix grammar: use “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add sharper differentiation by referencing scale or organizational complexity rather than listing channels.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex communications operations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Listing channels here overlaps with multiple experience bullets; keep the intro high-level and value-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Stakeholder coordination.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership competencies over task-level items; consider: Digital strategy & transformation • Editorial systems & governance • Web platform modernization • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-channel communications leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Stakeholder coordination • Multimedia & live event production
- Replace vague phrasing like “Workflow & systems architecture” with clearer, CV-aligned language such as “Content operations & workflow design” or “Digital systems & governance.”
- Keep British/American style consistent: use “communications” rather than “communication” to match the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Web & CMS administration” and analytics items repeat Topline Skills/Technical + IT; keep this section higher-level, not tool-adjacent.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, strategic outcomes, and only the newest/highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, campaign infrastructure, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; e.g., “Built Drupal campaign experiences and reusable content modules to support member storytelling, downloadable toolkits, and scalable microsite launches.”
- Reframe technical work at a higher level: replace “Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” with “Led platform enhancements, CMS implementation, and issue resolution for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add outcomes where possible: number of microsites/toolkits launched, workflow time saved, search relevance gains, adoption by teams, or performance improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital systems, workflows and analytics” and “governance… across web, email, social and multimedia” repeat themes already covered in the 2022–2024 Director role.
- The AI search and microsite details also duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level if those projects remain below.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the biggest transformation: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-focused; add metrics if available (open rates, follower growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings): “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials…”
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics and publishing infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language may duplicate the older advocacy video bullets unless framed here as studio-building and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct achievement-based position. Tighten it around what changed under your leadership and add any measurable growth if available.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Replace “helping” phrasing with direct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and standardized publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this role more execution/scale-focused, not enterprise leadership-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as expansion/operationalization rather than initial creation.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” is stronger than listing multiple CMSs first.
- Prioritize recent/high-value skills; move older or secondary platforms later.
- Tighten wording and group related items for readability.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences • WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages”

Suggested edit:

- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI design and dashboarding • Executive reporting and decision support • SEO and digital performance analysis”
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to outcomes from the 2022–2024 role, such as supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add context on level of use or be trimmed to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to another section or drop it if usage was light.
- Add a light qualifier to show depth, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages**.
- If formatting allows, rename to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner alignment with the rest of the CV.
- Keep it concise; avoid listing tools here that are better covered under coding/technical implementation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modernize older terms where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript (incl. jQuery) • API and third-party integrations • Google Tag Manager implementation • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • CI/CD and deployment automation (GitHub Actions)**
- Consider grouping by function rather than listing tools randomly; this makes the section feel more senior and intentional.
- If accurate, replace broad terms with stronger specifics: e.g., **REST APIs**, **custom GTM event tracking**, **build/deployment workflows**, or **performance/security scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears in Topline Skills; keep the fuller detail here and shorten/remove it there.
- **API integrations** and workflow/automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more strategic by separating automation tools from collaboration platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance to recent work and leadership value: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were central to measurable improvements, reference outcomes in recent roles instead of here (e.g., workflow standardization, cross-team coordination, reduced manual steps).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are generic unless tied to operational impact elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, frame these as platforms used for member communications and engagement workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten/standardize phrasing: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add light context for impact: **Enterprise/member email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider ordering by recency/strength of use rather than brand recognition.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat audience-size claims here unless you add distinct capability language.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than strategic.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs or scale you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience reach, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, specify tools/platforms or ownership level (e.g., managed publishing calendar, led livestream production, trained junior staff).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or piloting the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced member engagement.
- Consider a stronger action/result version: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, establishing an early multimedia channel for member and policy communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support + first podcast.
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia work already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
